findings.description: The 'data' bucket declares no ACL, no public access block, and no bucket policy restricting access; the inline comment confirms it is intended to be public. A public bucket holding the customer master file exposes sensitive data to anonymous readers/writers.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects such as customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
The bucket has no logging block, so no audit trail exists for reads or writes of the sensitive customer data it stores, hindering detection of unauthorized access.
Versioning is disabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be permanently overwritten or deleted with no recovery path — a data integrity/destruction risk amplified by the bucket being public.
A customer master spreadsheet (likely PII) is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is unencrypted and publicly accessible, and the object itself sets no kms_key_id or server-side encryption.
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial records stored unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured for the financials bucket, so access to financial data is not auditable.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, allowing irrecoverable deletion or tampering of financial objects.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with the bucket, so a later ACL or bucket policy change could expose it publicly without a defence-in-depth guardrail.
The operations bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, so stored objects are not encrypted with a managed key by default.
No logging block is configured, leaving no S3 server access log trail for this bucket.
No public access block resource restricts ACLs or policies on this bucket, removing an account-level guardrail against accidental public exposure.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so analytics datasets are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against ACL or policy changes that would make it publicly readable.

The log destination bucket uses force_destroy = true with no public access block, object lock, or bucket policy enforcing aws:SecureTransport; audit logs can be destroyed wholesale, undermining forensic integrity.
No bucket policy denies non-TLS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests, so log data may be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP. The same gap applies to all buckets in this file.
